A clear left-to-right object sequence on ivory paper: stack of tan fibre-textured tiles labelled 'Keratin'; arrow to small brass scissors symbol labelled 'Keratinase' cutting ONE tile into small fragments; arrow to a small pile of fragments labelled 'Nutrients'; arrow to a simple teal branching thread with extending tip arrows labelled 'Fungal growth'. teaching.question: Why do dermatophytes preferentially colonise keratinised material?
teaching.answer: They can enzymatically break down and use keratin as a nutrient source, supporting growth in keratinised skin, hair and nails.

title: Keratin can feed dermatophyte growth
caption: Dermatophytes can use keratin as a nutrient source. Enzymatic breakdown helps explain their affinity for keratinised material in skin, hair and nails.
alt: Keratin-labelled tiles are broken into nutrient pieces by a scissor-shaped enzyme symbol, feeding a simple growing fungal filament.
